content:
leah_m: quick follow-up from the loader-RFC: proposal for a manifest-driven prefetch quorum + soft-fallback shim for safetensors sharded models. want to lock down interface and telemetry before I update the RFC.

sanjay_r: can you sketch the quorum idea? sounds heavy.

leah_m: idea: each shard can have multiple mirrors/variants listed in the manifest (primary, mirrors, compact-variant). prefetch succeeds when we obtain a configured quorum (e.g., majority or N-of-M) of shard replicas for safety. If quorum can't be met within timeout, two options: (A) return a runtime shim that provides read-only synthetic tensors derived from a compact variant or cached prefix (soft-fallback), or (B) fail-hotstart and route to cold-serving. goal: avoid half-mapped tensors.

nina_s: how would the runtime shim behave? do ops see different dtypes? will layernorm blow up?

leah_m: shim contract: it must present identical tensor shapes and key names. dtype can differ but manifest must include a `shim_transform` describing on-the-fly conversion (example: `int8-q4` -> dequantize to float16 with scale table). shim must expose a warning metric so we can detect quality changes.

tom_b: hmm, building dequant inline raises perf concerns. maybe only allow shim for small embedding tables, not large attention weights. we need manifest flags: `shim_allowed: ["embedding","bias"]` etc.

sanjay_r: what about correctness? some optimizations rely on exact fp16 layout (qkv packing). shim could be incompatible. we need a manifest `compatibility_level` enum: `BINARY_COMPAT`, `SEMANTIC_CONVERTIBLE`, `NO_SHIM`. loader refuses shim unless `SEMANTIC_CONVERTIBLE`.

leah_m: yep — manifest example: "shard_entry": {"path":"...","mirrors":["s3://a","s3://b"],"checksum":"...","compat_level":"SEMANTIC_CONVERTIBLE","shim_allowed":["embedding","layernorm"]}. also include `fetch_priority` per mirror.

nina_s: mirrors + quorum solve noisy network issues. what's quorum default? majority? N-of-M?

tom_b: make it policy-driven: `quorum_policy` in hotstart config: `ALL`, `MAJORITY`, `ANY_N` (with N). default MAJORITY. ops can lower to ANY_N for PLG to reduce tail latency.

sanjay_r: good. but fallback storms are concerning. propose per-model circuit-breaker: `hotstart_credits` tokens refilled slowly. if exhausted, route new requests to cold-serving and mark model `degraded=true`.

leah_m: agree. add token-bucket id tied to model_id+region. infra-bot: can we reuse existing rate-limiter infra for this?

infra-bot: yes. can create a `hotstart-token-bucket` keyed by `model_id` in the quota service. default refill: 1 token per minute, burst 5. API available.

nina_s: telemetry plan? we need to know how often shim used and whether outputs diverge.

leah_m: telemetry: `hotstart.event` with fields: `result` in [ok_quorum, shim_used, failed, timeout, corrupt], `requested_shards`, `fetched_replicas`, `shim_type`, `quorum_policy`. Also `hotstart.quality_delta` linking to eval delta when eval gating used.

tom_b: eval gating: if shim_used and model is pinned, require fast eval check before permitting production traffic. if eval delta > threshold, auto-escalate to oncall. For PLG models, log only.

sanjay_r: need checksum semantics: do we checksum per-replica or per-logical-shard after assembly? prefer both: per-replica quick check and a final assembled-shard checksum. manifest should include both `replica_checksum` and `assembled_checksum`.

leah_m: implemented as: fetch replicas -> verify replica_checksum -> assemble/merge -> verify assembled_checksum -> commit mapping. failure at any step triggers fallback.

nina_s: what about rolling updates to shard layout (repartitioning)? old nodes may have cached older assembled_checksum. we need a cache-invalidation header in manifest with `generation` and `compatible_generations` to allow graceful hot-swap.

leah_m: add `generation:int` and `incompatible_after:int` fields. loader refuses stale caches if generation mismatch. background backfill can attempt swap when new generation fully present.

tom_b: operations: rollout plan = feature-flag `hotstart_quorum_v2` with default `MAJORITY` in canaries, gather metrics for two weeks, then flip for workers. include chaos tests that kill primary mirrors to ensure fallback paths exercised.

sanjay_r: tests: unit tests for quorum logic, integration tests with s3-mock for mirror failover, perf microbench verifying shim overhead for embedding-only shim. also an e2e synthetic model that exercises assembled_checksum mismatch.

leah_m: API surface changes: loader config additions: `quorum_policy`, `hotstart_timeout_ms`, `hotstart_credits_key`, `allow_shim:boolean`, and manifest additions described above. default behavior: MAJORITY, hotstart_timeout_ms=2500, allow_shim=false for pinned models? maybe true for PLG.

nina_s: I'd default `allow_shim=false` for production models and allow teams to opt-in. safer.

tom_b: one more: swap semantics. if shim used then later assembled replica becomes available, swap must be atomic and invalidate KV/attention caches. add a `swap_state` hook: `prepare_swap() -> quiesce_inflight() -> commit_swap() -> kvcache.invalidate(keys)`. runtime must implement quiesce within T_swap milliseconds.

leah_m: will write state machine in RFC: START -> RESOLVE_MANIFEST -> PREFETCH_REPLICAS -> VERIFY_REPLICAS -> ASSEMBLE -> VERIFY_ASSEMBLED -> COMMIT -> RETURN. On failure: depending on policy -> TRY_SHIM -> or ROUTE_COLD. Swap path documented separately.

infra-bot: CI: loader-quorum-tests running... all green (45s).

leah_m: action items: (1) i'll update RFC with manifest schema + state machine + swap hooks; (2) sanjay to draft token-bucket integration; (3) tom to write shim performance microbench; (4) nina to author telemetry + eval gating plan.

sanjay_r: ack, will PR token-bucket adapter.

tom_b: will add microbench in perf repo.

nina_s: will start telemetry PR, include alert when `shim_used_rate > 0.05%` for pinned models.

leah_m: thanks folks — will post the RFC revision here when ready. :rocket:
